entries.text: A jail, a prisoner, a town and a siege — the film the pack's collapse test cannot dislodge, because removing the contested claim and the force that settles it leaves nothing at all. Hawks made it in explicit disagreement with High Noon, replacing a marshal who asks for help with one who declines it and a community that fails with a group that is sufficient. Professional competence is offered as the complete answer to the moral question the other film asks.

entries.name: The Man Who Shot Liberty Valance (1962 film)
entries.author: dir. John Ford
entries.awards: Nominated for one Academy Award at the thirty-fifth ceremony (1963) for 1962 films — Costume Design, Black-and-White. No win.
entries.description: Statehood, the ballot and the gun, with the territory's founding act reassigned in a flashback the town never hears. The film is the genre's own…
entries.text: Statehood, the ballot and the gun, with the territory's founding act reassigned in a flashback the town never hears. The film is the genre's own verdict on itself: it prints the legend, tells you it is printing the legend, and declines to withdraw it. It is an adaptation — Dorothy M. Johnson's short story of 1949 is the original — and the famous line about printing the legend is the film's, not hers.

entries.name: Warlock
entries.author: Oakley Hall
entries.awards: Often described as a Pulitzer nominee; the Pulitzer published no fiction finalists before 1980 and the pack could find no primary source, so it asserts nothing.
entries.description: A town hires its own law and then cannot dislodge it, which is the whole book: miners, deputies, a mining company and a citizens' committee all…
entries.text: A town hires its own law and then cannot dislodge it, which is the whole book: miners, deputies, a mining company and a citizens' committee all holding warrants, none of them quite legitimate. Hall wrote it as a deliberate demolition of the Earp legend and of the genre's assumption that a hired gun can be a solution. It is the revision arriving in prose eleven years before Peckinpah, and the western the pack most often finds itself needing when a card wants a case where every claimant is partly right.

entries.name: Welcome to Hard Times
entries.author: E. L. Doctorow
entries.description: A town destroyed by one man in an afternoon, rebuilt out of nothing but the will to hold the ground, and destroyed again — a first novel written, by…
entries.text: A town destroyed by one man in an afternoon, rebuilt out of nothing but the will to hold the ground, and destroyed again — a first novel written, by the author's own account, out of contempt for the western screenplays he was reading as a studio reader. It is the anti-western rather than the revisionist western: it does not correct the form's history, it denies that the settlement had any content at all. The 1967 film shares the title and almost nothing else.

entries.name: Butcher's Crossing
entries.author: John Williams
entries.description: A Harvard man funds a buffalo hunt into a Colorado valley and the party kills until there is nothing left to kill and no market left to sell to. It…
entries.text: A Harvard man funds a buffalo hunt into a Colorado valley and the party kills until there is nothing left to kill and no market left to sell to. It is one of the pack's admitted costs and the card shows the working: there is no rival claimant and no contest over title, so it is admitted on force and on lineage — the force being the slaughter itself and the collapse of the hide price. What it demolishes is the idea that the frontier was a place where labour and land met productively.

entries.name: The Wild Bunch
entries.author: dir. Sam Peckinpah
entries.awards: Nominated for two Academy Awards at the forty-second ceremony (1970) for 1969 films — Story and Screenplay, and Original Score. No wins.
entries.description: A railroad, an army payroll and a Mexican federal general: three claims to the same money, and all three illegitimate. The film is the point at…
entries.text: A railroad, an army payroll and a Mexican federal general: three claims to the same money, and all three illegitimate. The film is the point at which the genre's violence stops being a settlement and becomes a spectacle it is uneasy about, staged in multi-camera slow motion assembled by the editor Lou Lombardo on the example of Bonnie and Clyde rather than, as is usually said, taken from Kurosawa. Its men are professionals whose only remaining principle is that they finish what they contract to do.

entries.name: Little Big Man (1970 film)
entries.author: dir. Arthur Penn
entries.awards: Nominated for one Academy Award at the forty-third ceremony (1971) for 1970 films — Chief Dan George for Supporting Actor, the first Academy Award nomination for an Indigenous North American actor. No win. He did win the New York Film Critics Circle and National Society of Film Critics awards for the role.
entries.description: A hundred-and-twenty-one-year-old narrator crosses back and forth between two societies, through the Washita at the midpoint and on to the Little…
entries.text: A hundred-and-twenty-one-year-old narrator crosses back and forth between two societies, through the Washita at the midpoint and on to the Little Bighorn at the end, and the film's shifts between farce and horror are the mechanism rather than a tonal problem. It is the Vietnam-era revision at its most legible, with Custer as a figure of vanity and the cavalry as an instrument of destruction. Chief Dan George's performance is the film's centre; he was the first Indigenous North American actor nominated for an Academy Award, and he won the New York Film Critics Circle and National Society of Film Critics awards for it.

entries.name: McCabe & Mrs. Miller
entries.author: dir. Robert Altman
entries.awards: Nominated for one Academy Award at the forty-fourth ceremony (1972) for 1971 films — Julie Christie for Actress. No win.
entries.description: A zinc-mining town's title bought out by a company that subcontracts the gun work, which makes it the clearest statement in the pack that the force…
entries.text: A zinc-mining town's title bought out by a company that subcontracts the gun work, which makes it the clearest statement in the pack that the force settling the claim can be corporate and salaried. McCabe is not killed in a duel; he is killed by three men doing a job while the town saves its church from a fire and does not notice. The famous ending, snow and opium and nobody watching, is the genre's most complete refusal of the walk-down.

entries.name: Centennial
entries.author: John Wilder
entries.awards: Nominated for one Primetime Emmy Award in 1979 — Outstanding Art Direction for a Limited Series or Special. No win.
entries.description: Miniseries. Two centuries of a single Colorado valley's title, from Arapaho occupancy through fur trade, cattle, irrigation and sugar beet to…
entries.text: Miniseries. Two centuries of a single Colorado valley's title, from Arapaho occupancy through fur trade, cattle, irrigation and sugar beet to agribusiness and the water table — twenty-six hours of television about who holds ground and how they came to. Its length is the argument: the settlement is shown as a sequence of transfers rather than as an arrival. Adapted from James A. Michener's 1974 novel, which is the original.

entries.name: Heaven's Gate
entries.author: dir. Michael Cimino
entries.description: The Johnson County War: a stockgrowers' association draws up a list of people to be killed, and the state ratifies it. It is the most literal…
entries.text: The Johnson County War: a stockgrowers' association draws up a list of people to be killed, and the state ratifies it. It is the most literal ground-claim film in the American canon and its commercial failure has been allowed to stand in for a critical judgement for forty years. The animal cruelty on the production is documented and led directly to the restoration of the American Humane Association's on-set authority, which the association had held since 1940 and lost in 1980; the pack states it on the card rather than in a footnote.

entries.name: Blood Meridian
entries.author: Cormac McCarthy
entries.description: Scalp bounties as the settlement's accounting, in a novel that follows the historical Glanton gang across the borderlands in 1849 and 1850 and…
entries.text: Scalp bounties as the settlement's accounting, in a novel that follows the historical Glanton gang across the borderlands in 1849 and 1850 and declines to supply a moral position from which to watch. It is admitted on force and on lineage: there is no contest between claimants, only the extraction of a price per head, and the book is written in explicit relation to the genre it is dismantling. It is also carded in the historical and literary packs, which is intentional and never deduped — Western cards it from the Western contract or not at all.

entries.name: Unforgiven
entries.author: dir. Clint Eastwood
entries.awards: Won four Academy Awards at the sixty-fifth ceremony (1993) for 1992 films — Best Picture, Best Director, Gene Hackman for Supporting Actor and Film Editing. Also won the Western Heritage Award (Wrangler) for Theatrical Motion Picture at the 1993 ceremony.
entries.description: A bounty raised by prostitutes against a sheriff's private jurisdiction, in a town where the law is whatever Little Bill decides it is and the…
entries.text: A bounty raised by prostitutes against a sheriff's private jurisdiction, in a town where the law is whatever Little Bill decides it is and the gunfighter is a drunk who cannot mount his horse. Every myth the genre sells is priced and then shown not to work: the reputation is a story a hack writer made up, the killing is squalid, and the man who does it says so. It is one of the small number of westerns to win Best Picture — three or four depending on whether No Country for Old Men is counted — and the one that did it by taking the form apart.

entries.name: Dead Man
entries.author: dir. Jim Jarmusch
entries.awards: None (verified negative); it competed for the Palme d'Or at Cannes in 1995.
entries.description: A machine town owned outright by the man whose name is on it, and a clerk from Cleveland who arrives to find the job already filled and is shot…
entries.text: A machine town owned outright by the man whose name is on it, and a clerk from Cleveland who arrives to find the job already filled and is shot within the hour. Nobody, the Blackfoot man who reads him as the poet William Blake, supplies the counter-reading the film runs on, and the Indigenous dialogue is unsubtitled on purpose. It is the film on which Jonathan Rosenbaum built his account of the acid western, which makes it the theoretical centre of a subgenre assembled after the fact.

entries.name: Deadwood
entries.author: David Milch
entries.awards: Won eight Primetime Emmy Awards from twenty-four nominations across its run, including Directing for a Drama Series in 2004 for Walter Hill.
entries.description: An illegal camp on Lakota treaty land, where there is no law at all to hold title and every arrangement is therefore a private one, enforced by…
entries.text: An illegal camp on Lakota treaty land, where there is no law at all to hold title and every arrangement is therefore a private one, enforced by whoever can. It is the purest statement in the pack of the question the whole pack is organised around — whose claim, and what warrant — because the answer is openly nobody's, and the characters know it and negotiate accordingly. The elaborate register is a deliberate choice: the flat screen-western idiom would have sounded modern.

entries.name: Hell on Wheels
entries.author: Joe and Tony Gayton
entries.awards: Nominated for one Primetime Emmy Award in 2012 — Outstanding Original Main Title Theme Music, for Gustavo Santaolalla. No win.
entries.description: The Union Pacific's right-of-way driven across treaty land, with Black, Irish and Cheyenne claims all live at once and the railroad itself as the…
entries.text: The Union Pacific's right-of-way driven across treaty land, with Black, Irish and Cheyenne claims all live at once and the railroad itself as the force that settles them. It is the rare screen western in which the antagonist is a construction schedule and the money behind it, and in which the freedman's claim to wages and the Cheyenne claim to the ground are shown as the same argument conducted at different scales. Uneven across five seasons, and the first two are where the pack's material is.

entries.name: Godless
entries.author: Scott Frank
entries.awards: Won three Primetime Emmy Awards at the seventieth ceremony (2018), including Jeff Daniels for Supporting Actor in a limited series.
entries.description: Miniseries. A New Mexico mining town whose men were killed in a single accident, leaving the women holding the title alone against a mining company…
entries.text: Miniseries. A New Mexico mining town whose men were killed in a single accident, leaving the women holding the title alone against a mining company and a gang. The premise is the pack's own claim structure with the usual claimant removed, which is what makes it useful: the question of who may hold ground is asked of people the genre normally files as dependants. It is also a corrective to the assumption that the revision ended in the 1970s.

entries.category: The Elegiac and the Late Western
entries.name: Monte Walsh
entries.author: Jack Schaefer
entries.description: Open range enclosed by wire and by eastern capital, and a cowhand whose claim is to a job that is being abolished around him. The force here is the…
entries.text: Open range enclosed by wire and by eastern capital, and a cowhand whose claim is to a job that is being abolished around him. The force here is the balance sheet: the outfit is bought by a syndicate, the syndicate is run from a long way off, and the work goes. Schaefer wrote it fourteen years after Shane and it is the exact inverse — no hero arrives, nothing is settled, and the man's competence is the thing that has stopped being worth anything.

entries.category: The Elegiac and the Late Western
entries.name: The Shootist
entries.author: Glendon Swarthout
entries.description: A gunman with terminal cancer claims a room, a doctor's honesty and the manner of his own death, in an El Paso of January 1901 that has electric…
entries.text: A gunman with terminal cancer claims a room, a doctor's honesty and the manner of his own death, in an El Paso of January 1901 that has electric streetcars and no further use for him; the 1976 film moves it to Carson City, and the film's setting is routinely reported as the novel's. The premise is stated with complete economy in the first pages and then followed to its least comfortable conclusion with no reprieve arranged. It is the elegiac western's cleanest single statement, and the 1976 film's casting made it a statement about something else as well.

entries.category: The Elegiac and the Late Western
entries.name: Lonesome Dove
entries.author: Larry McMurtry
entries.awards: Won the Pulitzer Prize for Fiction in 1986 for the 1985 novel.
entries.description: A cattle drive from the Rio Grande to Montana, undertaken for no reason anyone can defend, at a cost the book counts precisely. The pack cards it…
entries.text: A cattle drive from the Rio Grande to Montana, undertaken for no reason anyone can defend, at a cost the book counts precisely. The pack cards it against the grain of its own organising claim, because the Montana ground is not contested by anybody: it is admitted on lineage, and it is a western about the price of a claim nobody is disputing. McMurtry wrote it partly to demolish the myth and watched it become the myth's most beloved modern text, which is a reception inversion the card states.

entries.category: The Elegiac and the Late Western
entries.name: Lonesome Dove (1989 tv)
entries.author: Bill Wittliff
entries.awards: Nominated for eighteen Primetime Emmy Awards in 1989 and won seven. It did not win Outstanding Miniseries, which is the award most often attributed to it.
entries.description: Miniseries. The adaptation that made the novel a national event, and the pack's standing example of the medium trap this genre sets: it is…
entries.text: Miniseries. The adaptation that made the novel a national event, and the pack's standing example of the medium trap this genre sets: it is television, not film, and is catalogued as a film constantly. Wittliff's script keeps the book's structure almost intact across four parts, which is why it works where two-hour compressions of the same material do not. Its success produced a sequel not written by McMurtry, which is a separate object again.

entries.category: The Elegiac and the Late Western
entries.name: Broken Trail
entries.author: Alan Geoffrion
entries.awards: Won Primetime Emmy Awards at the fifty-ninth ceremony (2007), including Outstanding Miniseries.
entries.description: Television film. A horse drive intersected by the trafficking of five Chinese women, which gives the block its one live contested claim — the…
entries.text: Television film. A horse drive intersected by the trafficking of five Chinese women, which gives the block its one live contested claim — the women's claim to their own persons, against a purchase the law of the moment does not disturb. Walter Hill directs it flatly and without ceremony, and the film's refusal to make the rescue heroic is what keeps it from sentimentality. It is a television film, not a film, which is the same trap the entry above sets.

entries.category: The Elegiac and the Late Western
entries.name: Red Dead Redemption
entries.author: Rockstar San Diego
entries.awards: Won multiple industry awards in 2018 and 2019; it did not win Game of the Year at The Game Awards in 2018, which went to God of War, and the pack states that rather than the vaguer claim.
entries.description: 1911, and a former outlaw coerced by federal agents into hunting down the men he rode with — the closing of his own era, performed by him, under…
entries.text: 1911, and a former outlaw coerced by federal agents into hunting down the men he rode with — the closing of his own era, performed by him, under duress. The elegiac western's structure survives the transfer to a medium where the player is the one doing the closing, and the fact that the coercion is the mission structure is the point rather than an irony. It is the strongest single case in the pack for the argument that a mechanic can carry a genre's argument.

entries.category: The Elegiac and the Late Western
entries.name: Red Dead Redemption 2
entries.author: Rockstar Studios
entries.awards: Won multiple industry awards in 2010 and 2011, including Game of the Year at the Spike Video Game Awards and from BAFTA's Games committee.
entries.description: 1899: the range closing, the Pinkertons arriving, and a gang with nowhere left to be. It collapses cleanly on force and on lineage, and its subject…
entries.text: 1899: the range closing, the Pinkertons arriving, and a gang with nowhere left to be. It collapses cleanly on force and on lineage, and its subject is the same one the late prose westerns take — the moment at which a way of holding ground stops being available and the people holding it have no second trade. Its labour conditions during production are documented and are part of the record of the object.

entries.name: The Life of Hon. William F. Cody, Known as Buffalo Bill
entries.author: William F. Cody
entries.description: Memoir. The primary document in which a man converts his own contested biography into a saleable claim, published while he was performing a stage…
entries.text: Memoir. The primary document in which a man converts his own contested biography into a saleable claim, published while he was performing a stage version of it. The authorship is itself contested — the extent of the ghostwriting is not settled — which makes the book a legend-and-fact case in its own composition as well as its content. Everything downstream, the dime novels, the arena show and eventually the film industry's whole western apparatus, descends from this act of self-documentation.

entries.name: The Man Who Shot Liberty Valance
entries.author: Dorothy M. Johnson
entries.description: Short story. Statehood, the ballot, and which of two claims to a killing the territory is going to print. The story is the original and is regularly…
entries.text: Short story. Statehood, the ballot, and which of two claims to a killing the territory is going to print. The story is the original and is regularly displaced by the 1962 film in accounts of the material; it was published in Cosmopolitan in June 1949, and the commonly cited 1953 is the date of the Indian Country collection. The line about printing the legend is the film's invention, not hers, which is worth knowing before quoting it as her verdict.

entries.name: They Died with Their Boots On
entries.author: dir. Raoul Walsh
entries.description: Custer manufactured as a martyr defending a treaty he had in fact broken, with Errol Flynn riding to the Little Bighorn as a man keeping his word to…
entries.text: Custer manufactured as a martyr defending a treaty he had in fact broken, with Errol Flynn riding to the Little Bighorn as a man keeping his word to the Lakota. It is the legend at its industrial peak and it is worth studying precisely because it is not cynical: the film believes what it is selling. Set against Little Big Man thirty years later, it measures the distance the genre travelled, and it is the counter-case the pack keeps for any argument that the western was always self-aware.

entries.name: The Assassination of Jesse James by the Coward Robert Ford
entries.author: Ron Hansen
entries.description: Celebrity as the contested property, and force as a bullet followed by a stage show in which the killer re-enacts the killing nightly until someone…
entries.text: Celebrity as the contested property, and force as a bullet followed by a stage show in which the killer re-enacts the killing nightly until someone kills him. The novel's method is accumulation of documented detail until the legend has no room left to stand in, and its title states the verdict the whole book then complicates. The 2007 film is a close adaptation and the pack carries them as separate entries.

entries.name: Buffalo Bill and the Indians, or Sitting Bull's History Lesson
entries.author: dir. Robert Altman
entries.awards: Won the Golden Bear at the Berlin International Film Festival in 1976.
entries.description: The Wild West show staged as the exact moment at which a settlement becomes a product, with the payroll, the rehearsals and the contract…
entries.text: The Wild West show staged as the exact moment at which a settlement becomes a product, with the payroll, the rehearsals and the contract negotiations treated as the real subject and the performance as the by-product. Sitting Bull is present as an employee whose refusal to perform the version required of him is the film's only act of resistance. Adapted from Arthur Kopit's 1968 play Indians, which is the original.

entries.name: The Lone Ranger
entries.author: Fran Striker and George W. Trendle
entries.description: Radio series. The template for the second mode, assembled at a Detroit station and running for over two thousand episodes: a mask, a code written…
entries.text: Radio series. The template for the second mode, assembled at a Detroit station and running for over two thousand episodes: a mask, a code written down as a creed, a silver bullet, and a Native companion whose standing the format never once examines. No claim to ground is contested in it, because the moral order is settled before each episode begins and the work is enforcement rather than adjudication. Everything the character became — serials, television, comics and at least four feature films — descends from this radio original, which is regularly skipped in accounts that start at 1949.

entries.name: Gunsmoke
entries.author: John Meston and Norman Macdonnell
entries.description: Radio series. Dodge City jurisdiction, written for sound: the landscape is built entirely in effects, the violence is ugly, and its aftermath is…
entries.text: Radio series. Dodge City jurisdiction, written for sound: the landscape is built entirely in effects, the violence is ugly, and its aftermath is played rather than cut away from. The marshal is tired rather than heroic and the doctor is used as the show's conscience. The description of it as the first adult western originates in CBS's own marketing rather than in any critical finding, and the pack states it as marketing rather than repeating the priority claim.

entries.name: Fort Laramie
entries.author: Kathleen Hite and Norman Macdonnell
entries.description: Radio series. A cavalry post and the enforcement of treaties the government intends to break, made by the people who had already built Gunsmoke and…
entries.text: Radio series. A cavalry post and the enforcement of treaties the government intends to break, made by the people who had already built Gunsmoke and lasting a single season; Macdonnell produced and directed, and Kathleen Hite wrote twenty-seven of its forty-one episodes, which is the credit this card exists to keep visible. It is the rare western that makes the institution's own paperwork the source of the drama: the captain's problem is usually an order rather than an enemy. Its brevity is a fact about network scheduling rather than about quality, and it is the best surviving evidence of what the adult radio western could do with the cavalry material.

entries.name: Frontier Gentleman
entries.author: Antony Ellis
entries.description: Radio series. A correspondent for the Times of London rides through the American West and files what he sees, which makes the whole series an…
entries.text: Radio series. A correspondent for the Times of London rides through the American West and files what he sees, which makes the whole series an outside witness structure — radio's own revisionist experiment, arriving a decade before the films. The device lets the show decline to resolve what it reports. Also a single season, and also a consequence of the network schedule rather than of the writing.

entries.name: The Lone Ranger (1949 tv)
entries.author: George W. Trendle
entries.description: The radio property transferred to television, and the point at which the western became children's programming as a matter of industrial fact rather…
entries.text: The radio property transferred to television, and the point at which the western became children's programming as a matter of industrial fact rather than of critical opinion. Clayton Moore's mask and Jay Silverheels's Tonto are the images the second mode has circulated ever since, largely detached from any story. Silverheels was Mohawk, from Six Nations of the Grand River, and his career is the pack's clearest instance of an Indigenous actor employed continuously inside a format that gave him nothing to hold.

entries.name: Gunsmoke (1955 tv)
entries.author: John Meston and Norman Macdonnell
entries.awards: Won five Primetime Emmy Awards — Best Dramatic Series and Editing in 1958, Dennis Weaver for Supporting Actor in 1959, Milburn Stone for Supporting Actor in 1968, and Sound Editing in 1970.
entries.description: Twenty seasons, the longest run of any American television western and long enough that the series is really three different shows. The early…
entries.text: Twenty seasons, the longest run of any American television western and long enough that the series is really three different shows. The early half-hour episodes carry the radio version's grimness; the later hour-long seasons are a different and softer object. Its longevity is the single best measure of how completely the western owned American television, and its cancellation in 1975 is the conventional marker for when that stopped.

entries.name: Have Gun – Will Travel
entries.author: Sam Rolfe and Herb Meadow
entries.awards: Nominated for Primetime Emmy Awards during its run, including Richard Boone in 1959 and 1960, with no win. Gene Roddenberry won a Writers Guild of America award for the episode "Helen of Abajinian".
entries.description: Force sold by contract, from a San Francisco hotel, by a man who quotes literature and prices the job — the professional plot in weekly instalments,…
entries.text: Force sold by contract, from a San Francisco hotel, by a man who quotes literature and prices the job — the professional plot in weekly instalments, and the clearest television statement of the position Will Wright named. Paladin's card is the show's whole thesis: a claim to violence advertised, negotiated and invoiced. It is also one of the very few westerns to transfer from television to radio rather than the other way round, which is the collision the pack's namespace has to handle.

entries.name: Maverick
entries.author: Roy Huggins
entries.awards: Won a Primetime Emmy Award for a western series at the eleventh ceremony (1959).
entries.description: The genre laughing at its own code while keeping every piece of its furniture, with a hero who would rather leave than fight and says so. It is the…
entries.text: The genre laughing at its own code while keeping every piece of its furniture, with a hero who would rather leave than fight and says so. It is the second mode arriving on television inside the saturation itself, and its parodies of rival programmes are the earliest sustained evidence that the audience knew the conventions well enough for the joke to work. Huggins built the show on the premise that a gambler's motives are legible in a way a marshal's are not.

entries.name: The Rifleman
entries.author: Arnold Laven, developed by Sam Peckinpah
entries.awards: Nominated for two Primetime Emmy Awards in 1959 — Best Western Series, and Johnny Crawford for Supporting Actor. No wins.
entries.description: A homestead in New Mexico Territory held by a widower with a modified Winchester and a son, which makes it a title-and-succession show rather than a…
entries.text: A homestead in New Mexico Territory held by a widower with a modified Winchester and a son, which makes it a title-and-succession show rather than a lawman show. The creator credit is itself disputed in the reference record — Laven is generally credited as creator with Peckinpah developing the property — and Peckinpah wrote several of the first season's episodes, where the apprenticeship is visible. The rifle's rate of fire is often called physically impossible: the mechanism is a set screw in an enlarged lever loop and works; what is impossible is the twelve consecutive rounds sometimes fired from a seven-round magazine.

entries.name: Bonanza
entries.author: David Dortort
entries.awards: Won three Primetime Emmy Awards — Colour Consultant in 1965, Film Editing in 1966, and Music Composition in 1971.
entries.description: The Ponderosa is a thousand square miles whose title is never once seriously contested across fourteen seasons, which is exactly why the pack cards…
entries.text: The Ponderosa is a thousand square miles whose title is never once seriously contested across fourteen seasons, which is exactly why the pack cards it: it is the settlement presented as settled, with the ranch as a moral position rather than a business. The drama is imported weekly from outside and then repelled. It was among the early American series shot in colour, which is a commercial fact that shaped the genre's look on television for a decade.

entries.name: Rawhide
entries.author: Charles Marquis Warren
entries.description: The trail drive as a weekly workplace, which makes it the occupational entry in the 1959 television saturation, the peak year of the form on…
entries.text: The trail drive as a weekly workplace, which makes it the occupational entry in the 1959 television saturation, the peak year of the form on American television; the often-quoted count of thirty prime-time westerns is repeated everywhere and sourced nowhere, and the pack does not state a number. The cattle, the water, the crew's wages and the trail boss's authority are the recurring subjects, and the show is the closest television came to Andy Adams. It is also where Clint Eastwood was working when Leone hired him, which is the transfer point between two of the pack's traditions.

entries.name: Little House on the Prairie (1974 tv)
entries.author: Michael Landon
entries.awards: Won four Primetime Emmy Awards — Cinematography in 1978 for Ted Voigtlander, and Music Composition in 1979, 1980 and 1982 for David Rose.
entries.description: The books turned into a family drama that ran nine seasons and detached almost completely from its source, keeping the homestead and discarding the…
entries.text: The books turned into a family drama that ran nine seasons and detached almost completely from its source, keeping the homestead and discarding the argument. What the novel states plainly — that the family was on Osage land and left when the army enforced the treaty — the series has no mechanism for saying. It is the second mode operating on material whose first-mode content is a matter of public record, which is a more interesting failure than a simple sentimentalisation.

entries.name: Lucky Luke
entries.author: Morris
entries.awards: None (verified negative for the first appearance).
entries.description: Bande dessinée. The second mode in its purest European form: every piece of the iconography catalogued, drawn with affection and reproduced without…
entries.text: Bande dessinée. The second mode in its purest European form: every piece of the iconography catalogued, drawn with affection and reproduced without any of the argument underneath it. The man who shoots faster than his shadow rides through a West assembled entirely from other westerns, and from 1955 René Goscinny's scripts made the historical citation part of the joke. It has sold in the hundreds of millions of albums across Europe and is largely unread in the United States, which is itself a finding about how the iconography travels.

entries.name: Tex
entries.author: Gian Luigi Bonelli and Aurelio Galleppini
entries.awards: None (verified negative for the first appearance).
entries.description: Comic strip. A Texas Ranger who marries a Navajo woman and becomes a Navajo chief, published monthly in Italy since 1948 and still running, which…
entries.text: Comic strip. A Texas Ranger who marries a Navajo woman and becomes a Navajo chief, published monthly in Italy since 1948 and still running, which makes it the longest continuously published western comic anywhere. Its pro-Indigenous line predates the Italian film cycle by nearly twenty years and is a corrective to any account in which Italy's interest in the western begins with Leone. It is also the evidence that the Italian cycle arrived in a country where the western had already been domestic for a generation.

entries.name: Blueberry
entries.author: Jean-Michel Charlier and Jean Giraud
entries.awards: None (verified negative for the first album).
entries.description: Bande dessinée. Apache treaty negotiation and cavalry command, begun as Fort Navajo and turning openly revisionist from around 1970, with the…
entries.text: Bande dessinée. Apache treaty negotiation and cavalry command, begun as Fort Navajo and turning openly revisionist from around 1970, with the protagonist deserting the army whose uniform he started in. Giraud stated his acquisition of Ford's compositions and later of Leone's, which makes the series a documented case of the lineage travelling into another medium and another language. Its draughtsmanship is the reason the European western looks the way it does.

entries.name: Jonah Hex
entries.author: John Albano and Tony DeZuniga
entries.awards: None (verified negative for the first appearance).
entries.description: Comic strip. A disfigured Confederate bounty hunter whose face is the story's whole moral apparatus, arriving in mainstream American comics at…
entries.text: Comic strip. A disfigured Confederate bounty hunter whose face is the story's whole moral apparatus, arriving in mainstream American comics at exactly the moment the revision was arriving in the cinema. The character is a genre object rather than a person and the strip knows it. It is the pack's evidence that the revisionist turn was general across media rather than a film-industry event.

entries.name: The Oregon Trail
entries.author: Don Rawitsch, Bill Heinemann and Paul Dillenberger
entries.description: The settlement argument implemented as a resource-management simulation for a school teletype, in which the player buys oxen, fords rivers and dies…
entries.text: The settlement argument implemented as a resource-management simulation for a school teletype, in which the player buys oxen, fords rivers and dies of dysentery. The people already on the ground appear as a trading opportunity or as weather, which is not a bias in the writing but a consequence of the model: they are not agents in the simulation at all. It is the pack's clearest case of a mechanic carrying an ideology, and it taught the settlement story to several generations of American schoolchildren.

entries.name: Desperados: Wanted Dead or Alive
entries.author: Spellbound Entertainment
entries.description: A real-time tactics game built on the Italian cycle's silhouettes and its assembled-crew structure, in which each character is a specific capability…
entries.text: A real-time tactics game built on the Italian cycle's silhouettes and its assembled-crew structure, in which each character is a specific capability and the level is a puzzle about combining them. It is second mode throughout: the iconography is the interface, and no claim to ground is in play. The pack cards it as the cleanest demonstration that the cycle's visual grammar had become a set of assets that could be assigned to a game designer as a brief.

entries.name: Call of Juarez: Gunslinger
entries.author: Techland
entries.description: An old bounty hunter tells his story in a bar and the level changes around the player as he corrects himself, which turns the genre's…
entries.text: An old bounty hunter tells his story in a bar and the level changes around the player as he corrects himself, which turns the genre's legend-and-fact problem into a mechanic the player is inside. When the narrator revises a detail the geometry revises with it. It is the most sophisticated thing any western game has done with the form's own preoccupations, and it does it in a shooter of about four hours.

entries.name: Weird West
entries.author: WolfEye Studios
entries.description: A mining company's claim worked through five separate protagonists whose stories intersect, in a West with a supernatural layer that never displaces…
entries.text: A mining company's claim worked through five separate protagonists whose stories intersect, in a West with a supernatural layer that never displaces the economic one. It is the pack's exhibit for the weird western as a standpoint rather than a setting: the strange material is what lets the game say what the company is doing. The immersive-simulation design means the player's solutions are their own, which is a different relationship to the genre's violence than a scripted western offers.

entries.name: Black Elk Speaks
entries.author: Black Elk, as told to John G. Neihardt
entries.description: Memoir. Lakota treaty land, the Ghost Dance and Wounded Knee, told by a man who was there and written down by a poet who shaped what he heard. The…
entries.text: Memoir. Lakota treaty land, the Ghost Dance and Wounded Knee, told by a man who was there and written down by a poet who shaped what he heard. The as-told-to authorship is a live scholarly problem rather than a technicality: Neihardt's editorial hand, his framing and his ending have all been examined against the stenographic record, and the pack states the dispute rather than presenting the book as unmediated testimony. Much of the vocabulary the genre later borrowed and hollowed out passes through this text.

entries.name: We Pointed Them North
entries.author: E. C. Abbott and Helena Huntington Smith
entries.description: Memoir. A trail hand's own account of the work: wages, injuries, brothels, the price of a horse, and the composition of the crews — which is the…
entries.text: Memoir. A trail hand's own account of the work: wages, injuries, brothels, the price of a horse, and the composition of the crews — which is the evidence that puts paid to the assumption that the cattle West was white. Teddy Blue Abbott dictated it to a journalist late in life and the collaboration is on the title page. The pack's working specialist runs on this book more than on any other single source, because it is the rare document written from inside the labour rather than about it.

entries.name: With His Pistol in His Hand
entries.author: Américo Paredes
entries.description: Narrative history. The corrido of Gregorio Cortez read as a counter-record: a manhunt, a mistranslated word, and a Texas Ranger version of events…
entries.text: Narrative history. The corrido of Gregorio Cortez read as a counter-record: a manhunt, a mistranslated word, and a Texas Ranger version of events the ballad flatly contradicts. Paredes treats the song's variants as evidence rather than as corruption, which is the methodological move that founded borderlands studies. His case against the Rangers' record is a scholarly argument with named opponents and the pack states it as an argument.

entries.name: Bury My Heart at Wounded Knee
entries.author: Dee Brown
entries.description: Narrative history. A treaty-by-treaty accounting of the settlement from 1860 to 1890, assembled from council records and testimony, which reached a…
entries.text: Narrative history. A treaty-by-treaty accounting of the settlement from 1860 to 1890, assembled from council records and testimony, which reached a mass readership at the moment the revision was reaching the cinema. Its influence on what the genre could afterwards assume is larger than its standing among specialists, several of whom have criticised its structure and its sources. Both facts belong on the card.

entries.name: The Legacy of Conquest
entries.author: Patricia Nelson Limerick
entries.description: Narrative history. The New Western History's central statement, and the pack's authority for retiring frontier as an analytic term: it is a process…
entries.text: Narrative history. The New Western History's central statement, and the pack's authority for retiring frontier as an analytic term: it is a process word that functions only from the settler's side, and conquest, place and continuity are offered in its place. The insistence that the western story does not end in 1890 is what licenses this pack's neo-western material. The pack uses the word frontier throughout as the name of the myth under study, which is the distinction her argument makes available.

entries.category: The Neo-Western and the Modern West
entries.name: The Brave Cowboy
entries.author: Edward Abbey
entries.description: A man with no draft card, no social security number and no papers of any kind claims the right to move across a New Mexico that has been fenced,…
entries.text: A man with no draft card, no social security number and no papers of any kind claims the right to move across a New Mexico that has been fenced, paved and administered while he was not looking. The force that settles it is a highway, a jeep and a helicopter, which is the neo-western's whole argument stated in its first important book. It was filmed in 1962 as Lonely Are the Brave, under a different title, so the two do not collide in the pack's namespace.

entries.category: The Neo-Western and the Modern West
entries.name: Horseman, Pass By
entries.author: Larry McMurtry
entries.description: Ranch title passing to an heir who intends to sell it, with the crisis supplied by a federal hoof-and-mouth cull that destroys the herd the title is…
entries.text: Ranch title passing to an heir who intends to sell it, with the crisis supplied by a federal hoof-and-mouth cull that destroys the herd the title is worth anything for. McMurtry's first novel, written at twenty-five, and already carrying his standing position: the cattle West is a business that failed, and the people mourning it are mourning a wage. Filmed in 1963 as Hud, under a different title.

entries.category: The Neo-Western and the Modern West
entries.name: The Last Picture Show
entries.author: Larry McMurtry
entries.description: A north Texas town with nothing left in it, in which the closing of the cinema is the last thing to happen. There is no claim to ground at all: what…
entries.text: A north Texas town with nothing left in it, in which the closing of the cinema is the last thing to happen. There is no claim to ground at all: what the book documents is the aftermath, the settled country as an emptied one, and the pack cards it as the neo-western's account of what the settlement produced. The 1971 film is a close adaptation and the two are separate entries.

entries.category: The Neo-Western and the Modern West
entries.name: Brokeback Mountain
entries.author: Annie Proulx
entries.awards: Won the National Magazine Award for Fiction in 1998 and third prize in the O. Henry Awards in 1998.
entries.description: Short story. Two men employed to watch sheep on a Wyoming mountain in 1963, and the twenty years afterwards in which neither can arrange a life. The…
entries.text: Short story. Two men employed to watch sheep on a Wyoming mountain in 1963, and the twenty years afterwards in which neither can arrange a life. The pack's collapse test does not break it — remove the contested ground and the force and the story stands — so it is handed to the literary-reference pack and Western keeps only the residual: the cowboy as the genre's own figure of unfitness, working a job the myth does not describe. It was published in The New Yorker in October 1997; the 2005 film is the adaptation.

entries.category: The Neo-Western and the Modern West
entries.name: No Country for Old Men
entries.author: Cormac McCarthy
entries.description: Drug money in a case in the desert, a man who takes it, and a sheriff who narrates his own obsolescence in italics between the chapters. It does not…
entries.text: Drug money in a case in the desert, a man who takes it, and a sheriff who narrates his own obsolescence in italics between the chapters. It does not collapse on the ground clause — nobody's claim to land is in dispute — and the pack admits it on the lineage clause alone, which the card says rather than smuggling. What it inherits from the western is the border, the pursuit, the sheriff and the conviction that the country used to make sense.

entries.category: The Neo-Western and the Modern West
entries.name: No Country for Old Men (2007 film)
entries.author: dir. Joel and Ethan Coen
entries.awards: Won four Academy Awards at the eightieth ceremony (2008) for 2007 films — Best Picture, Best Director, Adapted Screenplay, and Javier Bardem for Supporting Actor.
entries.description: A close adaptation admitted on the same terms as the novel, and one of the small number of westerns by any definition to win Best Picture — which…
entries.text: A close adaptation admitted on the same terms as the novel, and one of the small number of westerns by any definition to win Best Picture — which the pack's own count has to state carefully, because whether it is a western at all is the argument the entry exists to have. Its violence is almost entirely elided or heard rather than shown. The sheriff's closing speech is the novel's, delivered flat, and the film ends on it without resolution.

entries.category: The Neo-Western and the Modern West
entries.name: Justified
entries.author: Graham Yost
entries.awards: Won Primetime Emmy Awards during its run, including Margo Martindale for Supporting Actress in 2011.
entries.description: A deputy US marshal's jurisdiction transplanted to Harlan County, Kentucky, which makes it the neo-western's cleanest jurisdiction case: federal…
entries.text: A deputy US marshal's jurisdiction transplanted to Harlan County, Kentucky, which makes it the neo-western's cleanest jurisdiction case: federal authority operating inside a place with its own older arrangements about who settles what. Raylan Givens's quick-draw is played as an anachronism the department cannot discipline out of him. It is built from Elmore Leonard's novella "Fire in the Hole", whose first publication year the pack could not fix and does not state, and Leonard's dialogue method is the show's stated model throughout.

entries.category: The Neo-Western and the Modern West
entries.name: Longmire
entries.author: Hunt Baldwin and John Coveny
entries.awards: Won the Western Heritage Award (Wrangler) at the 2013 ceremony. Nominated for an Edgar Award and a PRISM Award.
entries.description: A Wyoming county sheriff and the Cheyenne tribal police whose jurisdiction overlaps his, which is the entire premise rather than a recurring…
entries.text: A Wyoming county sheriff and the Cheyenne tribal police whose jurisdiction overlaps his, which is the entire premise rather than a recurring complication — the show is about two legal systems occupying one map. It is the most sustained treatment on television of concurrent jurisdiction as a dramatic engine, and it employs Native actors in the roles that carry that half of it. Adapted from Craig Johnson's novels, which are the original.

entries.category: The Neo-Western and the Modern West
entries.name: Hell or High Water
entries.author: dir. David Mackenzie
entries.awards: Nominated for four Academy Awards at the eighty-ninth ceremony (2017) for 2016 films, including Best Picture and Original Screenplay. No wins.
entries.description: A reverse-mortgaged Texas ranch reclaimed by robbing the branches of the bank that holds the lien, which restores the range war exactly and puts a…
entries.text: A reverse-mortgaged Texas ranch reclaimed by robbing the branches of the bank that holds the lien, which restores the range war exactly and puts a bank where the cattleman used to be. The force settling the claim is a financial instrument, and the film is unusually precise about how the instrument works. Written by Taylor Sheridan, whose subject throughout is a frontier moral vocabulary meeting modern paperwork and losing.

entries.category: The Neo-Western and the Modern West
entries.name: The Rider
entries.author: dir. Chloé Zhao
entries.awards: Won the Art Cinema Award in the Directors' Fortnight at Cannes in 2017. No major-ceremony nominations.
entries.description: A rodeo rider on Pine Ridge with a head injury that means he cannot ride again, played by a man to whom that happened, alongside his own family. It…
entries.text: A rodeo rider on Pine Ridge with a head injury that means he cannot ride again, played by a man to whom that happened, alongside his own family. It is the pack's model case for admission on force rather than on violence: nothing is settled by a gun, and what takes the claim away is a fracture and an economy with no second job in it. The Lakota cast are non-professionals playing versions of themselves, which is the film's method and also its ethical problem, and the card names both.

entries.category: The Neo-Western and the Modern West
entries.name: Yellowstone
entries.author: Taylor Sheridan
entries.awards: Kevin Costner won the Golden Globe for Best Actor in a Television Drama in 2023. Its Primetime Emmy record is thin relative to its audience, which is itself part of the record.
entries.description: A Montana ranch title held against a developer, a tribal land claim and the state itself, by a family that treats homicide as an estate-management…
entries.text: A Montana ranch title held against a developer, a tribal land claim and the state itself, by a family that treats homicide as an estate-management tool. It is the modern land-claim western with the politics left in and no attempt to make the holders sympathetic on any ground except possession. Its politics are argued over in ways the show mostly declines to settle, and the size of its audience is itself a finding about what the genre can still do.

entries.category: The Neo-Western and the Modern West
entries.author: Taylor Sheridan
entries.awards: Sam Elliott won the Screen Actors Guild Award for a male actor in a television movie or limited series in 2023. Nominated for two Primetime Emmy Awards in 2022.
entries.description: A Reconstruction-era wagon train to a Montana claim, written as the origin of the title contested in the present-day series, which makes the pair…
entries.text: A Reconstruction-era wagon train to a Montana claim, written as the origin of the title contested in the present-day series, which makes the pair the genre's most explicit statement that a modern claim is only as good as the violence that established it. The trail is filmed as attritional rather than adventurous. It is the rare prequel whose function is to indict the thing it precedes rather than to ennoble it.

entries.name: The Life and Adventures of Joaquín Murieta
entries.author: John Rollin Ridge
entries.description: Californio title extinguished by the 1851 Land Act and by mob force, written by a Cherokee man whose family emigrated west voluntarily in 1837,…
entries.text: Californio title extinguished by the 1851 Land Act and by mob force, written by a Cherokee man whose family emigrated west voluntarily in 1837, ahead of the removal, and who later left for California after killing David Kell at Bentonville, Arkansas, in 1849 in the aftermath of the treaty-party feud. It is generally described as the first novel published by a Native American author, and it is the genre's earliest counter-text, and the fact that it is about Mexican rather than Cherokee dispossession is the point: Ridge writes conquest from inside one, about another. The Murieta of every later retelling, including Zorro's ancestry, comes out of this book.

entries.name: Cogewea, the Half-Blood
entries.author: Mourning Dove
entries.description: Ranch and allotment title on the Flathead, and a heroine excluded from both sides of her descent by machinery that is legal rather than violent —…
entries.text: Ranch and allotment title on the Flathead, and a heroine excluded from both sides of her descent by machinery that is legal rather than violent — the force here is allotment law and the marriage market. The book enters both races at a fair, the Ladies' Race and the Squaw Race, wins both and is refused both purses, which is the pack's most compact image of staged authenticity. How far Lucullus V. McWhorter rewrote it is a live scholarly dispute the card states and does not settle.

entries.name: House Made of Dawn
entries.author: N. Scott Momaday
entries.awards: Won the Pulitzer Prize for Fiction, awarded in 1969 for the 1968 book.
entries.description: Pueblo land, the relocation programme, and a killing the court cannot read because the reasons for it are not available in the language the court is…
entries.text: Pueblo land, the relocation programme, and a killing the court cannot read because the reasons for it are not available in the language the court is conducted in. The force is federal Indian policy, applied to a returning veteran who is legally free and materially unable to occupy anything. It is the book that made Native-authored prose about the West impossible to ignore, and the Pulitzer's award year and the book's year are constantly merged.

entries.name: Winter in the Blood
entries.author: James Welch
entries.description: Reservation ranching on Fort Belknap — Welch was Blackfeet and A'aniiih and set the book on the latter's reservation, which is regularly reported as…
entries.text: Reservation ranching on Fort Belknap — Welch was Blackfeet and A'aniiih and set the book on the latter's reservation, which is regularly reported as Blackfeet — narrated by a man who cannot name what is wrong and whose losses are disclosed to the reader before they are to him. The claim is to standing on land the family legally holds and has materially lost the use of. Its flat comic surface over unresolved grief is the counter-western's most-copied register, and its refusal to explain anything to an outside reader is deliberate.

entries.name: Ceremony
entries.author: Leslie Marmon Silko
entries.description: Laguna land, uranium leasing and a veteran's return, with the cure and the land's condition treated as one operation rather than two subjects. The…
entries.text: Laguna land, uranium leasing and a veteran's return, with the cure and the land's condition treated as one operation rather than two subjects. The bomb was tested on ground adjacent to the pueblo and the ore came from underneath it, which the novel states as the fact it is. It is the ground-claim story told from the side that lost, using ceremony rather than force as the settlement, and it is the block's most-taught text.

entries.name: Smoke Signals
entries.author: dir. Chris Eyre
entries.awards: None (verified negative at the major ceremonies; it took the Audience Award and a Filmmakers Trophy at Sundance in 1998).
entries.description: A road movie from Coeur d'Alene to Phoenix and back with a jar of ashes, written by Sherman Alexie from his own stories and directed by Chris Eyre —…
entries.text: A road movie from Coeur d'Alene to Phoenix and back with a jar of ashes, written by Sherman Alexie from his own stories and directed by Chris Eyre — two claims the pack keeps apart. Its lineage is stated inside the film as acquisition: the line about Indians watching Indians on television is the genre being cited by the people it was made about. Alexie's later record is a matter of public dispute and belongs on the writing credit rather than on the direction.

entries.name: Atanarjuat: The Fast Runner
entries.author: dir. Zacharias Kunuk
entries.awards: Won the Caméra d'Or at Cannes in 2001 — a prize for a first feature, not a best-film award.
entries.description: Camp leadership and the right to a place in it, contested and settled by force and then by exile, in Inuktitut throughout with no settler frame at…
entries.text: Camp leadership and the right to a place in it, contested and settled by force and then by exile, in Inuktitut throughout with no settler frame at any point. Its lineage clause is deliberately absent, which is the card's whole interest: it is admitted on ground and force alone, and it demonstrates that the pack's third clause is a description of how the genre travelled rather than a requirement of the form. The naked run across the ice is the most-cited image, and the trial that follows it is the film's actual subject.

entries.name: Reservation Dogs
entries.author: Sterlin Harjo and Taika Waititi
entries.awards: Won a Peabody Award in 2022; nominated for Primetime Emmy Awards.
entries.description: Muscogee Nation land, four teenagers who want to leave it, and a grief none of them will name — with the force being poverty and jurisdiction rather…
entries.text: Muscogee Nation land, four teenagers who want to leave it, and a grief none of them will name — with the force being poverty and jurisdiction rather than any gun. Its writers' room and directing roster were Indigenous throughout, which is a production fact rather than a claim about representation and is the reason the show can be as unguarded as it is. Every piece of the genre's furniture survives in it as a joke.

entries.name: Prey
entries.author: dir. Dan Trachtenberg
entries.awards: Won one Primetime Emmy Award for Sound Editing, at the seventy-fifth Creative Arts ceremony held in January 2024.
entries.description: Comanche hunting ground in 1719, contested by French trappers and by something else, with a young woman who is refused the hunt taking it anyway. It…
entries.text: Comanche hunting ground in 1719, contested by French trappers and by something else, with a young woman who is refused the hunt taking it anyway. It is not Indigenous-directed, and what admits it to this block is the Comanche producer Jhane Myers, the largely Native cast, and the full Comanche-language dub released alongside the English version — the pack's exhibit for what a language track can do. The card names the direction credit rather than letting the block imply it.

entries.name: Dark Winds
entries.author: Graham Roland
entries.description: Navajo Nation jurisdiction, worked as the literal question of who may arrest whom and under whose warrant, which makes it the pack's cleanest…
entries.text: Navajo Nation jurisdiction, worked as the literal question of who may arrest whom and under whose warrant, which makes it the pack's cleanest jurisdiction case in any medium. Adapted from Tony Hillerman's novels by Graham Roland, a Chickasaw creator — John Wirth is the showrunner, and the two credits are separate — with a largely Native writers' room, which is the production answer to the outsider-authorship problem the source carries. The Navajo Nation named Hillerman a Special Friend of the Dineh in 1987, and the criticism of his authorship is also on the record; the card carries both.

entries.category: The Removal, the Reservation and the Wars
entries.name: A Man Called Horse
entries.author: Dorothy M. Johnson
entries.description: Short story. A Boston gentleman taken by a Crow band and held — the English lord and the Lakota belong to the 1970 film, not to Johnson, and the…
entries.text: Short story. A Boston gentleman taken by a Crow band and held — the English lord and the Lakota belong to the 1970 film, not to Johnson, and the substitution is one of the most reliable errors in writing about this story — in which the contested ground is a body and the force that settles the claim is captivity itself — the genre's oldest layer, written in twenty pages. Johnson's version is far more interested in what the captive learns than in what he escapes, and it ends without the vindication the adaptations supply. It was published in Collier's in 1950 and collected in Indian Country in 1953; the 1970 film is the adaptation and departs substantially.

entries.category: The Removal, the Reservation and the Wars
entries.name: Broken Arrow
entries.author: dir. Delmer Daves
entries.awards: Nominated for three Academy Awards at the twenty-third ceremony (1951) for 1950 films, including Story. No wins.
entries.description: Chiricahua title and the Jeffords negotiation, with the making of an agreement as the film's climax rather than a battle — the founding text of the…
entries.text: Chiricahua title and the Jeffords negotiation, with the making of an agreement as the film's climax rather than a battle — the founding text of the sympathetic-Indian studio cycle, and the limit of it: Cochise is played by Jeff Chandler and the marriage the film builds is killed off. Its screenplay was fronted by Michael Blankfort for the blacklisted Albert Maltz, the nomination stands under Blankfort's name, and the Writers Guild restored Maltz's credit in 1991. Adapted from Elliott Arnold's 1947 novel Blood Brother.

entries.category: The Removal, the Reservation and the Wars
entries.name: Little Big Man
entries.author: Thomas Berger
entries.description: A narrator who claims to be a hundred and eleven years old and to have been present at both the Washita and the Little Bighorn, on both sides, which…
entries.text: A narrator who claims to be a hundred and eleven years old and to have been present at both the Washita and the Little Bighorn, on both sides, which contests the claim twice over and makes the reliability of the whole account the book's real subject. Berger's Cheyenne material is researched and his Custer is a study in self-invention. The 1970 film takes the frame and sharpens the politics; the novel is funnier, longer and less certain.

entries.category: The Removal, the Reservation and the Wars
entries.name: Dances With Wolves
entries.author: dir. Kevin Costner
entries.awards: Won seven Academy Awards at the sixty-third ceremony (1991) for 1990 films, including Best Picture and Best Director.
entries.description: Lakota hunting ground and the army arriving to take it, filmed with subtitled Lakota rather than dubbed English — the decision that made the Lakota…
entries.text: Lakota hunting ground and the army arriving to take it, filmed with subtitled Lakota rather than dubbed English — the decision that made the Lakota characters people rather than obstacles, and the one the film is genuinely owed credit for. Doris Leader Charge coached the language and appears in the film, and Russell Means was among those who noted that the dialogue's gendered forms are wrong. The white-saviour reading is a live argument and the pack states both sides rather than settling it.

entries.category: The Removal, the Reservation and the Wars
entries.name: Into the West
entries.author: William Mastrosimone
entries.awards: Won two Primetime Emmy Awards at the fifty-eighth ceremony (2006) — Sound Mixing and Music Composition.
entries.description: Miniseries. Forty years of treaty, removal and reservation followed through two family lines, one white and one Lakota, so that the same events are…
entries.text: Miniseries. Forty years of treaty, removal and reservation followed through two family lines, one white and one Lakota, so that the same events are narrated twice from inside. Its length lets it do what a feature cannot: show the settlement as a sequence of documents and displacements rather than as a confrontation. It is television rather than film, which is the trap this genre sets more often than any other. Mastrosimone created it and four writers share the teleplays, of whom Kirk Ellis is the most often credited with the whole.

entries.category: The Removal, the Reservation and the Wars
entries.name: Bury My Heart at Wounded Knee (2007 tv)
entries.author: dir. Yves Simoneau
entries.awards: Won Primetime Emmy Awards at the fifty-ninth ceremony (2007), including Outstanding Made for Television Movie; accounts of the total differ between six and seven and the pack states neither.
entries.description: Television film. The Dawes Act and Wounded Knee, built around Charles Eastman as the figure who moves between the agency and the people it…
entries.text: Television film. The Dawes Act and Wounded Knee, built around Charles Eastman as the figure who moves between the agency and the people it administers, which narrows Dee Brown's continental accounting into a single argument about assimilation. It shares its title with the 1970 book and is a different object with a different structure; the pack's namespace disambiguates it. It is a television film, not a film.

entries.category: The Removal, the Reservation and the Wars
entries.name: Scalped
entries.author: Jason Aaron and R. M. Guéra
entries.awards: None (verified negative for the first issues).
entries.description: Comic strip. Casino land on the fictional Prairie Rose reservation, tribal sovereignty used as a business instrument, and an FBI jurisdiction that…
entries.text: Comic strip. Casino land on the fictional Prairie Rose reservation, tribal sovereignty used as a business instrument, and an FBI jurisdiction that does not fit the territory it is operating in. It is the most sustained treatment in comics of the contemporary jurisdictional West, and its authorship is non-Native on Lakota subject matter, which is a documented criticism the card states. The comic is the original; a later television adaptation is not carded here.

entries.name: The Life and Adventures of Nat Love
entries.author: Nat Love
entries.description: Memoir. The testimony that sits underneath every Black-cowboy card in the pack: a man born enslaved in Tennessee who worked the cattle country,…
entries.text: Memoir. The testimony that sits underneath every Black-cowboy card in the pack: a man born enslaved in Tennessee who worked the cattle country, wrote it down, and ended his working life as a Pullman porter. The force in it is the market for labour, and the claim is to standing. It is unreliable by design rather than by accident — it is written to assert competence — and its self-mythologising as Deadwood Dick collides with Edward L. Wheeler's fictional character of 1877, a collision the pack states and does not adjudicate.

entries.name: Buck and the Preacher
entries.author: dir. Sidney Poitier
entries.description: A freedmen's wagon train contesting its right to move west against labour recruiters sent to drag the migrants back to the plantations they left —…
entries.text: A freedmen's wagon train contesting its right to move west against labour recruiters sent to drag the migrants back to the plantations they left — force applied as gunfire and as contract, in the same plot. It is Poitier's directing debut, taken over from Joseph Sargent during production, and it is an explicit answer to the studio cycle rather than a variation on it: the cavalry is not coming, and the alliance that saves the train is with a band of Native people. The genre's furniture is used straight, which is what makes the argument land.

entries.name: Posse
entries.author: dir. Mario Van Peebles
entries.description: A freedmen's town and its title, against a white sheriff and a railroad that wants the ground it stands on — the deliberate reinsertion of Buffalo…
entries.text: A freedmen's town and its title, against a white sheriff and a railroad that wants the ground it stands on — the deliberate reinsertion of Buffalo Soldiers and all-Black townsites into the studio western's own iconography. The film frames itself with documentary material about the real towns, which states the lineage as correction rather than as homage. It is written by Sy Richardson and Dario Scardapane, and what is Van Peebles's is the direction.

entries.name: Night Song
entries.author: Beverly Jenkins
entries.description: A buffalo-soldier garrison, a Kansas schoolteacher, and a courtship conducted around the question of what standing either party has in the town —…
entries.text: A buffalo-soldier garrison, a Kansas schoolteacher, and a courtship conducted around the question of what standing either party has in the town — the Black West written inside a genre with a large readership and almost no presence in western reference books. Jenkins researches the historical record and appends her sources, which makes the novels a route into material the field otherwise leaves to specialists. The pack cards it from the Western contract; the romance-reference pack holds it on its own terms.

entries.name: The Harder They Fall
entries.author: dir. Jeymes Samuel
entries.awards: Won the BAFTA for Outstanding Debut by a British Writer, Director or Producer in 2022, for Jeymes Samuel. Won NAACP Image Awards for Outstanding Motion Picture and Outstanding Ensemble Cast.
entries.description: Rufus Buck's claim on a town, pursued by an assembled cast of documented Black westerners — Nat Love, Bill Pickett, Stagecoach Mary, Cherokee Bill —…
entries.text: Rufus Buck's claim on a town, pursued by an assembled cast of documented Black westerners — Nat Love, Bill Pickett, Stagecoach Mary, Cherokee Bill — in a plot that never happened, with a title card at the start saying exactly that. It is a second-mode work about first-mode figures: the iconography is in free circulation and the people inside it were real. Samuel directed and scored it and shares the screenplay credit with Boaz Yakin.

entries.name: Lawmen: Bass Reeves
entries.author: Chad Feehan
entries.awards: No wins; nominated at the Creative Arts Emmys and for Black Reel and Astra awards.
entries.description: A federal deputy marshal's jurisdiction in Indian Territory, which is the pack's question in its most literal form: who could arrest whom, under…
entries.text: A federal deputy marshal's jurisdiction in Indian Territory, which is the pack's question in its most literal form: who could arrest whom, under whose warrant, on whose land. Reeves was born enslaved, served under Judge Parker's court out of Fort Smith, and made thousands of arrests in a territory where the legal map was contested at every point. The claim that he is the original of the Lone Ranger is Art T. Burton's hypothesis and the pack cards it as a hypothesis rather than as fact.

entries.name: Ramona
entries.author: Helen Hunt Jackson
entries.description: Californio and Indigenous title extinguished after 1848 — the novel's Alessandro is Luiseño, of Temecula, and the Cahuilla attribution is a common…
entries.text: Californio and Indigenous title extinguished after 1848 — the novel's Alessandro is Luiseño, of Temecula, and the Cahuilla attribution is a common slip — written to do for federal Indian policy what Uncle Tom's Cabin had done for slavery. The reception inverted the argument completely: it produced a Southern California tourist industry, a pageant and a hotel trade, and no policy change at all. Jackson died in August 1885, a year after publication and before most of that had happened, so the pack states the inversion as the book's afterlife rather than as something she lived to see; what she did record was disappointment at how it was being read. The pack cards the inversion rather than the intention, which makes it the clearest case in the library of a book's afterlife defeating its author.

entries.name: Allá en el Rancho Grande
entries.author: dir. Fernando de Fuentes
entries.awards: Widely reported as taking a Venice photography prize in 1938 for Gabriel Figueroa; Venice had no cinematography category then and its own record for that year lists a special recommendation, so the pack states the report and not the award.
entries.description: The hacienda's claim on the people who work it, settled by patronage and by song rather than by the gun — the founding comedia ranchera and the film…
entries.text: The hacienda's claim on the people who work it, settled by patronage and by song rather than by the gun — the founding comedia ranchera and the film that made the charro a national figure and an export. It is the pack's demonstration that a settlement argument can be conducted entirely through obligation. Its politics are conservative and were read as such at the time, against de Fuentes's own revolutionary trilogy of the preceding years.

entries.name: The Ballad of Gregorio Cortez
entries.author: dir. Robert M. Young
entries.awards: No major-ceremony wins; Rosanna DeSoto won a Golden Eagle Award for her performance.
entries.description: A mistranslated word about a horse, a sheriff dead, and a manhunt across Texas conducted by hundreds of men — with the film deliberately withholding…
entries.text: A mistranslated word about a horse, a sheriff dead, and a manhunt across Texas conducted by hundreds of men — with the film deliberately withholding subtitles from the Spanish so that an English-speaking audience experiences the gap that killed him. It is built directly on Américo Paredes's 1958 study, which is a documented acquisition rather than a coincidence of subject. The court is the force that finally settles the claim, and it does so twice, in opposite directions.

entries.name: All the Pretty Horses
entries.author: Cormac McCarthy
entries.awards: Won the National Book Award for Fiction and the National Book Critics Circle Award for Fiction, both for 1992.
entries.description: A Texas ranch sold out from under the boy who expected to inherit it, and a claim re-attempted across the border where it is refused by a Mexican…
entries.text: A Texas ranch sold out from under the boy who expected to inherit it, and a claim re-attempted across the border where it is refused by a Mexican family with older money and then by a Mexican jail. It is McCarthy at his most accessible and it is still an argument about property: everything the boy wants is legally somebody else's. The horse knowledge is the only competence the book allows him, and it is not enough.

entries.name: Lone Star
entries.author: dir. John Sayles
entries.awards: Nominated for one Academy Award at the sixty-ninth ceremony (1997) for 1996 films — John Sayles for Original Screenplay. No win.
entries.description: A skeleton in the desert, and a border county's entire title history litigated through the question of who put it there — Anglo, Mexican, Black and…
entries.text: A skeleton in the desert, and a border county's entire title history litigated through the question of who put it there — Anglo, Mexican, Black and Kickapoo claims all live, across three generations, in a town where the past is a municipal argument about a school syllabus. Sayles cuts between decades within single shots rather than by dissolve, which puts the history inside the present frame. Its last line is the pack's best short statement of what the neo-western wants.

entries.name: The Three Burials of Melquiades Estrada
entries.author: dir. Tommy Lee Jones
entries.awards: Won two prizes at Cannes in 2005 — Best Actor for Tommy Lee Jones and Best Screenplay for Guillermo Arriaga.
entries.description: The right of a dead man to lie in his own ground, enforced privately at gunpoint by a friend who abducts the border patrolman that killed him and…
entries.text: The right of a dead man to lie in his own ground, enforced privately at gunpoint by a friend who abducts the border patrolman that killed him and marches him and the body into Mexico. It is the ground clause reduced to its smallest possible object — a grave — and the crossing is made in the direction the genre almost never films. Arriaga wrote it and Jones directed and starred, and the two claims are separate.

entries.category: Women, Labour and the Unmythic West
entries.name: O Pioneers!
entries.author: Willa Cather
entries.description: Nebraska title held and then enlarged by a woman's judgement about soil, against the advice of every man in the book — with the force being the…
entries.text: Nebraska title held and then enlarged by a woman's judgement about soil, against the advice of every man in the book — with the force being the mortgage, the drought and the length of time it takes. The stretch is visible and the card names it: nothing is settled by violence, and the violence that does arrive is domestic and irrelevant to the claim. It is the homestead western with the labour left in and the gunfight removed, which is the whole reason this category exists.

entries.category: Women, Labour and the Unmythic West
entries.name: Little House on the Prairie
entries.author: Laura Ingalls Wilder
entries.awards: None for this volume (verified negative; other books in the series took Newbery Honors).
entries.description: A homestead built on the Osage Diminished Reserve and abandoned when the army enforces the treaty — the settlement argument stated plainly, in a…
entries.text: A homestead built on the Osage Diminished Reserve and abandoned when the army enforces the treaty — the settlement argument stated plainly, in a children's book, by a narrator who does not think it needs defending. Everything the pack says about the ground clause is legible here in its most unguarded form, including a mother's stated opinion of the people whose land it is. The 1974 television series keeps the homestead and has no mechanism for saying any of this.

entries.category: Women, Labour and the Unmythic West
entries.name: The Time It Never Rained
entries.author: Elmer Kelton
entries.awards: Won the Spur Award for Best Western Novel in 1973, and a Western Heritage Award (Wrangler) at the 1974 ceremony.
