entries.description: The seven-year Texas drought of the 1950s, and a rancher who will not take the federal relief his neighbours take, until the land decides the…
entries.text: The seven-year Texas drought of the 1950s, and a rancher who will not take the federal relief his neighbours take, until the land decides the argument for him. The force is the weather and a farm programme, and the stretch is visible and stated. Kelton was an agricultural journalist for most of his working life, and it shows in the only way that matters: the book knows what things cost.

entries.category: Women, Labour and the Unmythic West
entries.name: The Homesman
entries.author: Glendon Swarthout
entries.awards: Won the Spur Award for Best Novel of the West in 1988 — the inaugural year of that category string, which is why searches for Best Western Novel in 1988 return nothing — and a Western Heritage Award (Wrangler).
entries.description: A woman holding a claim alone, and then contracted to freight four women the frontier has broken back east to their families — the cargo being the…
entries.text: A woman holding a claim alone, and then contracted to freight four women the frontier has broken back east to their families — the cargo being the thing the settlement produced and has no institutions for. The premise is stated in a page and followed without reprieve, which is Swarthout's method throughout. Its central reversal is one of the most brutal things in the genre and the card does not describe it.

entries.category: Women, Labour and the Unmythic West
entries.name: The Ballad of Little Jo
entries.author: dir. Maggie Greenwald
entries.description: A mining-camp claim that can only be held by a man, held by a woman living as one for the rest of her life — the force being the law of who may own…
entries.text: A mining-camp claim that can only be held by a man, held by a woman living as one for the rest of her life — the force being the law of who may own rather than anything with a trigger. It is based on Joe Monahan, whose sex was discovered after his death in 1904 and whose name the film respells as Monaghan, and it declines to treat the disguise as a caper. The most useful thing in it for the pack is the arithmetic: the film shows exactly what the alternative was.

entries.category: Women, Labour and the Unmythic West
entries.name: Meek's Cutoff
entries.author: dir. Kelly Reichardt
entries.awards: None (verified negative; it premiered at Venice in 2010).
entries.description: Passage, water, and whose account of the country to believe — three wagons on the high desert with a guide who is lost and a captive who may or may…
entries.text: Passage, water, and whose account of the country to believe — three wagons on the high desert with a guide who is lost and a captive who may or may not be leading them somewhere. It is the pack's model of admission on force rather than violence: nobody shoots anybody, and the coercion is total. The film is shot in the squarer Academy ratio to narrow what the women can see, and it ends without telling you, which is the argument.

entries.name: Thousand Pieces of Gold
entries.author: Ruthanne Lum McCunn
entries.description: Lalu Nathoy is sold in China, sold again into an Idaho mining camp, and ends holding a ranch on the Salmon River that the exclusion regime says she…
entries.text: Lalu Nathoy is sold in China, sold again into an Idaho mining camp, and ends holding a ranch on the Salmon River that the exclusion regime says she cannot own — a claim to ground and a claim to her own person contested in the same series of transactions. It is a biographical novel and the documentary record on the sale, the marriage and the ownership is thin and disputed, so the pack does not card its incidents as history. What it does card is the shape: the ground clause running through a person.

entries.name: How Much of These Hills Is Gold
entries.author: C Pam Zhang
entries.awards: Longlisted for the Booker Prize in 2020; not shortlisted and not a winner.
entries.description: Two children carry their father's body across a worked-out goldfield looking for ground to bury him in, which puts the prospecting claim, the burial…
entries.text: Two children carry their father's body across a worked-out goldfield looking for ground to bury him in, which puts the prospecting claim, the burial ground and the right to remain in the same opening chapter. The force is the Foreign Miners' Tax and the mob, and the landscape is a ruin rather than a promise. It is the strongest single card in this category and it is written from inside a family the genre has used as scenery for a century.

entries.name: Warrior
entries.author: Jonathan Tropper
entries.description: Chinatown ground, tong claims to it, and the San Francisco labour riots of the 1870s, in which the contested territory is a few streets and the…
entries.text: Chinatown ground, tong claims to it, and the San Francisco labour riots of the 1870s, in which the contested territory is a few streets and the force settling it is a mob with political backing. It is produced from a treatment by Bruce Lee, which is the other side of a documented origination dispute the pack states: Lee's family maintain the material behind Kung Fu was his, the studio account differs, and neither side has been adjudicated. Its subject is the standing of people the law of the period explicitly excluded.

entries.name: Robbery Under Arms
entries.author: Rolf Boldrewood
entries.description: Squatter title, cattle-duffing and the bushranger's counter-claim, narrated from the condemned cell by a man waiting to be hanged for it. It is the…
entries.text: Squatter title, cattle-duffing and the bushranger's counter-claim, narrated from the condemned cell by a man waiting to be hanged for it. It is the Australian tradition's founding prose. It was serialised in the Sydney Mail from 1882 and published as a book in 1888, and the pack cards the book year under its serialisation rule, which is why the familiar 1882 does not appear here. It arose alongside rather than out of the American popular western, which is the fact the card is for. The squatters' own title is shown to be an occupation rather than a grant, which the American form rarely admits this early.

entries.name: The Proposition
entries.author: dir. John Hillcoat
entries.awards: Won four Australian Film Institute Awards from twelve nominations in 2005.
entries.description: Frontier pacification in Queensland reduced to one police captain's private arithmetic: kill one brother to save another, on a deadline, with a…
entries.text: Frontier pacification in Queensland reduced to one police captain's private arithmetic: kill one brother to save another, on a deadline, with a family used as security. Nick Cave wrote it and has stated the Peckinpah and Leone acquisitions on the record, which makes the lineage documented rather than inferred. The Aboriginal characters are inside the plot rather than around it, and the film's violence is presented without any of the cycle's aestheticism.

entries.name: Sweet Country
entries.author: dir. Warwick Thornton
entries.awards: Won the Special Jury Prize at Venice in 2017 and the AACTA Award for Best Film in 2018.
entries.description: An Aboriginal stockman kills a white man in self-defence in the Northern Territory in the 1920s, and a travelling court is convened on the ground to…
entries.text: An Aboriginal stockman kills a white man in self-defence in the Northern Territory in the 1920s, and a travelling court is convened on the ground to decide what that was — station title, a manhunt and a trial, filmed in the genre's own grammar by a Kaytetye director. The film moves between English and Aboriginal language, which marks exactly who is permitted to be understood; the pack names no specific language here, having been unable to confirm which is used. It has no score at all, and it tells you the verdict before it gives you the argument.

entries.name: Mystery Road (2018 tv)
entries.author: Rachel Perkins
entries.awards: Won four AACTA Awards for its first series, including Best Television Drama Series.
entries.description: Outback jurisdiction, mining leases and an Aboriginal detective's standing with both the police and the community he is investigating — the…
entries.text: Outback jurisdiction, mining leases and an Aboriginal detective's standing with both the police and the community he is investigating — the Australian neo-western procedural, and the ground clause in its contemporary legal form. This card is the television series that began in 2018, not the 2013 feature of the same title, which the pack does not card. Ivan Sen made the features and is an executive producer here; the first series was directed by Rachel Perkins, and the two credits are separate. Each series is a self-contained case, and the country is filmed from the air until it stops looking like scenery.

entries.name: Per un pugno di dollari
entries.author: dir. Sergio Leone
entries.description: Released in English as A Fistful of Dollars. A man sells his services to both sides of a town split between two families, and the ground clause…
entries.text: Released in English as A Fistful of Dollars. A man sells his services to both sides of a town split between two families, and the ground clause fails outright: what is contested is money and a monopoly, not title. It is admitted on lineage, and the lineage is documented rather than inferred — Toho sued over the film's relation to Yojimbo and the matter was settled on reported terms rather than adjudicated. The Italian and English release years differ, which is the trap the pack's namespace exists to handle.

entries.name: Per qualche dollaro in più
entries.author: dir. Sergio Leone
entries.description: Released in English as For a Few Dollars More. Two bounty hunters working the same target, with a partnership structure the whole cycle then reused…
entries.text: Released in English as For a Few Dollars More. Two bounty hunters working the same target, with a partnership structure the whole cycle then reused and a vengeance plot restored underneath the money plot — the colonel is not in it for the price. Bounty is the cycle's standing substitute for title: the contested thing is a number on a poster. Luciano Vincenzoni's structural work is here, and the division of credit between him and Leone was publicly disputed by both for decades.

entries.name: Il buono, il brutto, il cattivo
entries.author: dir. Sergio Leone
entries.description: Released in English as The Good, the Bad and the Ugly. Gold replaces land, so the film does not collapse on the ground clause, and it is admitted on…
entries.text: Released in English as The Good, the Bad and the Ugly. Gold replaces land, so the film does not collapse on the ground clause, and it is admitted on lineage twice over — the Kurosawa acquisition behind the cycle and Leone's stated acquisition of Ford's compositions. The Civil War is walked through rather than fought, which is the cycle's characteristic relation to American history: it is scenery with a body count. The graveyard at the end is the cycle's most elaborate formal set-piece and the one most often reproduced.

entries.name: Django
entries.author: dir. Sergio Corbucci
entries.description: Mud, a coffin dragged through it, and a border town nobody has title to — the film the cycle's imitators returned to most openly, and the one that…
entries.text: Mud, a coffin dragged through it, and a border town nobody has title to — the film the cycle's imitators returned to most openly, and the one that most thoroughly abandons the western's landscape for a swamp. It is admitted on lineage. The name was never trademarked, which produced dozens of unofficial sequels with no connection to Corbucci, and none of them should be attributed to him; the pack's namespace keeps this entry separate from the 2012 and 2007 films that borrowed the name.

entries.name: Quién sabe?
entries.author: dir. Damiano Damiani
entries.description: Released in English as A Bullet for the General. The Zapata western's founding entry, and the one film in the cycle where land is explicitly the…
entries.text: Released in English as A Bullet for the General. The Zapata western's founding entry, and the one film in the cycle where land is explicitly the contested claim and the script says so out loud. An American attaches himself to a band of revolutionaries and turns out to be working for the government; the peasant leader understands this too late and the ending states the moral in a sentence. Damiani directed. The writing credit is layered rather than disputed: Salvatore Laurani holds the story and screenplay, and Franco Solinas is credited with the adaptation and dialogue, which is where the film's politics come from. Direction and writing are separate claims and the pack keeps them apart.

entries.name: Il grande silenzio
entries.author: dir. Sergio Corbucci
entries.description: Released in English as The Great Silence. Utah under snow, a bounty law that makes killing lawful, and outlaws who are outlaws because the law has…
entries.text: Released in English as The Great Silence. Utah under snow, a bounty law that makes killing lawful, and outlaws who are outlaws because the law has been written to make them so. It is the cycle's one full ground-and-law film: the contested question is which claims the state will recognise, and the state's answer is the atrocity. Its ending is the inversion the genre does not permit, and the alternative happy ending shot for certain markets is part of the record.

entries.name: C'era una volta il West
entries.author: dir. Sergio Leone
entries.description: Released in English as Once Upon a Time in the West. Water on the railroad's path, and a widow who inherits the one parcel the line must cross — the…
entries.text: Released in English as Once Upon a Time in the West. Water on the railroad's path, and a widow who inherits the one parcel the line must cross — the cycle's only unambiguous title contest, and its most American film. The story was written with Bernardo Bertolucci and Dario Argento out of named American westerns, which is documented acquisition rather than homage. It is also the cycle's own elegy: the man with the harmonica has no place in what the railroad is building and the film knows it.

entries.name: Il mercenario
entries.author: dir. Sergio Corbucci
entries.description: Released in English as The Mercenary. A Polish gunman hired to protect a mine, who ends up training a peasant revolt he has no politics about — the…
entries.text: Released in English as The Mercenary. A Polish gunman hired to protect a mine, who ends up training a peasant revolt he has no politics about — the Zapata western with the contract left visible and the ideology supplied by everybody except the protagonist. The story is Franco Solinas and Giorgio Arlorio's; the screenplay is Luciano Vincenzoni and Sergio Spina's, which is a four-name credit block regularly collapsed to one. Its bullfight-ring finale is the cycle's best single joke about spectacle.

entries.name: Giù la testa
entries.author: dir. Sergio Leone
entries.description: Released variously in English as Duck, You Sucker and A Fistful of Dynamite. A Mexican bandit and an Irish explosives man in the revolution, in…
entries.text: Released variously in English as Duck, You Sucker and A Fistful of Dynamite. A Mexican bandit and an Irish explosives man in the revolution, in Leone's most explicitly political film and his most disillusioned: the intellectual who reads Bakunin is shown what a revolution costs the people who did not choose it. It carries the cycle's terminal position, that the promise being fought over is a fraud. Its multiple English titles are themselves a namespace problem the pack solves by carding the Italian.

entries.category: The Ostern and the German West
entries.name: Winnetou 1. Teil
entries.author: dir. Harald Reinl
entries.description: Karl May filmed straight, in wide colour, for a mass European audience — the West German cycle that made the European western commercially serious…
entries.text: Karl May filmed straight, in wide colour, for a mass European audience — the West German cycle that made the European western commercially serious again, shot largely in Yugoslavia with a production arrangement the Italian cycle then used as well. Its Apache chief is played by a French actor and its German narrator is the moral centre, which is the arrangement DEFA was set up to answer. The postcard landscape and the blood-brotherhood are the whole content; none of the period's actual politics are present.

entries.category: The Ostern and the German West
entries.name: Neulovimye mstiteli
entries.author: dir. Edmond Keosayan
entries.description: Released in English as The Elusive Avengers. Four teenagers against an ataman's band on the southern steppe during the Civil War — the Soviet…
entries.text: Released in English as The Elusive Avengers. Four teenagers against an ataman's band on the southern steppe during the Civil War — the Soviet ostern's founding hit, produced in 1966 and released in 1967, which is the year the pack cards and the film that established the form's terms: the contested authority is revolutionary rather than juridical, and what is being settled is which order will govern rather than who holds a valley. The genre's furniture arrives wholesale, the politics are inverted, and the audience was enormous.

entries.category: The Ostern and the German West
entries.name: Die Söhne der großen Bärin (1966 film)
entries.author: dir. Josef Mach
entries.description: Dakota gold-treaty land and a Lakota leader defending it, in the film that opened the DEFA Indianerfilm cycle. Its lineage is a documented answer to…
entries.text: Dakota gold-treaty land and a Lakota leader defending it, in the film that opened the DEFA Indianerfilm cycle. Its lineage is a documented answer to Karl May: the brief was to make an anti-Winnetou, with Liselotte Welskopf-Henrich's research as the counter-source. The credit block carries the pack's whole international argument — a Czech director, an East German studio, a German woman's novels, a Serbian lead — and the redface problem is inseparable from the anti-colonial content, which the card states as both.

entries.category: The Ostern and the German West
entries.name: Chingachgook, die große Schlange
entries.author: dir. Richard Groschopp
entries.description: Delaware and Mohican land in 1740, adapted from Cooper's The Deerslayer — the setting predates the French and Indian War the DEFA material is…
entries.text: Delaware and Mohican land in 1740, adapted from Cooper's The Deerslayer — the setting predates the French and Indian War the DEFA material is usually filed under — by a state studio that was reversing his polarity on purpose — the founding American text acquired and turned around, which is the cleanest lineage acquisition in this category. The colonial powers are shown as two commercial interests using Indigenous nations against each other. It is the DEFA cycle answering the American canon directly rather than answering Karl May.

entries.category: The Ostern and the German West
entries.name: Beloye solntse pustyni
entries.author: dir. Vladimir Motyl
entries.awards: Awarded the Russian Federation State Prize in Literature and Arts — the 1997 prize, conferred in 1998, almost thirty years after release. It was passed over for the USSR State Prize in 1970.
entries.description: Released in English as White Sun of the Desert. A Red Army soldier trying to get home across Central Asia, made responsible for a harem he has no…
entries.text: Released in English as White Sun of the Desert. A Red Army soldier trying to get home across Central Asia, made responsible for a harem he has no idea what to do with. It does not collapse on the ground clause and is admitted on lineage: the cavalry western's grammar relocated to a desert where the contested authority is revolutionary. Its comic and elegiac registers run together, its songs carry the structure, and it became a national ritual object — watched by cosmonauts before launch, which is a fact about circulation rather than about the film.

entries.category: The Ostern and the German West
entries.name: Apachen
entries.author: dir. Gottfried Kolditz
entries.description: The 1837 killings at Santa Rita del Cobre — the Johnson scalp-hunting massacre of Mimbreño Apache — staged as the act of a mining company's men,…
entries.text: The 1837 killings at Santa Rita del Cobre — the Johnson scalp-hunting massacre of Mimbreño Apache — staged as the act of a mining company's men, with copper-mine title as the thing actually at stake. It is the DEFA cycle at its most historically specific and its most direct: the aggressor is commercial, the atrocity is the plot rather than the backstory, and the Apache lead carries the film's entire moral authority. It is one of a linked pair with Ulzana rather than the first of a series.

entries.category: Japanese Cinema and the Two-Way Traffic
entries.name: Shichinin no samurai
entries.author: dir. Akira Kurosawa
entries.awards: Won the Silver Lion at Venice in 1954. Nominated for two Academy Awards at the twenty-ninth ceremony (1957) — Art Direction and Costume Design, both black-and-white. No wins.
entries.description: Released in English as Seven Samurai. A village's rice and its right to keep it, defended by men hired for food because there is nothing else to pay…
entries.text: Released in English as Seven Samurai. A village's rice and its right to keep it, defended by men hired for food because there is nothing else to pay them with. The lineage runs both directions and both legs are documented: Kurosawa's own repeated statement of what he took from Ford, and the licensed remake as The Magnificent Seven in 1960, whose rights ran through Lou Morheim to Yul Brynner. The recruitment sequence is among the most reproduced structures in either genre.

entries.category: Japanese Cinema and the Two-Way Traffic
entries.name: Yojimbo
entries.author: dir. Akira Kurosawa
entries.awards: Won the Volpi Cup for Best Actor at Venice in 1961 for Toshiro Mifune.
entries.description: A town split between two claims and a man who sells force to both until neither is left, which is the plot the Italian cycle acquired and built a…
entries.text: A town split between two claims and a man who sells force to both until neither is left, which is the plot the Italian cycle acquired and built a decade on. The pack cards it as a separate entry from Per un pugno di dollari rather than folding the two together, because the traffic is the subject: this is the leg on which Toho sued and the matter was settled on reported terms. Its tone is comic in a way the remake is not, and the difference is where the two films' politics part.

entries.category: Japanese Cinema and the Two-Way Traffic
entries.name: Kōya no Shōnen Isamu
entries.author: Sōji Yamakawa and Noboru Kawasaki
entries.description: Manga. A boy of Japanese and American parentage in the American West, searching for a father he knows only by a scar — the studio western's…
entries.text: Manga. A boy of Japanese and American parentage in the American West, searching for a father he knows only by a scar — the studio western's iconography acquired wholesale for a weekly Japanese magazine, and then its plot. It is the clearest evidence that the traffic between Japan and the western ran through print as well as film, and that it ran in the decade the American genre was collapsing. The gunfighter arrives in Japanese comics as a fully formed set of conventions requiring no explanation.

entries.category: Japanese Cinema and the Two-Way Traffic
entries.name: Gun Frontier
entries.author: Leiji Matsumoto
entries.description: Manga. A Japanese swordsman and a drifter searching the West for immigrants who have disappeared, which puts a real presence argument underneath…
entries.text: Manga. A Japanese swordsman and a drifter searching the West for immigrants who have disappeared, which puts a real presence argument underneath what is otherwise second-mode play with the iconography. Matsumoto's West is assembled from other westerns and the people crossing it are the ones the American form never depicted. It is also the origin of a character pairing Matsumoto reused across his much better-known science-fiction work, which is the traffic running on again.

entries.category: Japanese Cinema and the Two-Way Traffic
entries.name: Trigun
entries.author: Yasuhiro Nightow
entries.description: Manga. Water rights on a desert colony world, contested between settlements that cannot all survive — the space western with the ground clause fully…
entries.text: Manga. Water rights on a desert colony world, contested between settlements that cannot all survive — the space western with the ground clause fully intact rather than decorative, which is rare in either tradition. The gunman at its centre has an enormous bounty and refuses to kill, so the plot is generated by the gap between his reputation and his practice. It is the pack's strongest case that the western's furniture can be relocated off Earth without the argument being lost.

entries.name: Winnetou I
entries.author: Karl May
entries.description: Apache land against a railway survey, narrated by a German surveyor who becomes the chief's blood brother — the founding text of the German western…
entries.text: Apache land against a railway survey, narrated by a German surveyor who becomes the chief's blood brother — the founding text of the German western and the single most consequential prose western written outside the United States, and the thing two later German film cycles were built to film and to answer. Lineage runs out of it rather than into it, which is what admits it. May had never been to the American West when he wrote it, served prison terms for fraud and impersonation, and for years presented himself in public as his own narrator; the German controversy over the books is live and the card names it.

entries.name: Umut
entries.author: dir. Yılmaz Güney
entries.awards: Won the second Adana Golden Boll festival in 1970, taking Best Film, Best Director, Best Screenplay, Best Actor and Best Cinematography; Best Actor at the Antalya Golden Orange; and a special prize at Grenoble. It was also banned in Turkey, which is a separate fact and not a gap in the award record.
entries.description: Released in English as Hope. An Adana carriage driver loses his horse and therefore his living, and goes looking for buried treasure with a hodja…
entries.text: Released in English as Hope. An Adana carriage driver loses his horse and therefore his living, and goes looking for buried treasure with a hodja and a divining rod. It is a western rather than neorealism because of a documented acquisition — the structure of The Treasure of the Sierra Madre, taken deliberately — and because the claim at issue is a means of subsistence that the road, the car and the police have already taken. The ending is the genre's bleakest statement of what a claim is worth without force behind it.

entries.name: Sholay
entries.author: dir. Ramesh Sippy
entries.awards: Won a Filmfare Award for Best Editing in 1976; its wider award record is thinner than its reputation.
entries.description: A retired policeman hires two convicts to take a village back from a dacoit who cut off his arms — village land held against a bandit, with the…
entries.text: A retired policeman hires two convicts to take a village back from a dacoit who cut off his arms — village land held against a bandit, with the stated acquisition being Leone and Shichinin no samurai together, which is the pack's own example of a lineage claim made by the film-makers rather than inferred by critics. It runs comedy, song, romance and massacre inside one picture, shot on thirty-five millimetre and blown up to seventy for release with stereophonic sound. Its original ending was changed by the censor board and later restored, so any description must name the cut it means.

entries.name: The Grey Fox
entries.author: dir. Phillip Borsos
entries.awards: Won seven Genie Awards from thirteen nominations in 1983, including Best Motion Picture and Best Achievement in Direction.
entries.description: A stagecoach robber released from San Quentin in 1901 into a British Columbia where the law arrived before the settlers did, which is the Northern's…
entries.text: A stagecoach robber released from San Quentin in 1901 into a British Columbia where the law arrived before the settlers did, which is the Northern's premise and the pack's clearest counter-example to the claim that the western is set in the gap before law. Bill Miner has no gap to work in: the Mounted Police are already there, the country is already surveyed, and the only crime available is the train. It is elegiac without being American about it.

entries.name: Five Fingers for Marseilles
entries.author: dir. Michael Matthews
entries.description: A South African township's land, taken twice — once under apartheid by the police, and again in the present by people who came out of the resistance…
entries.text: A South African township's land, taken twice — once under apartheid by the police, and again in the present by people who came out of the resistance to the first taking. The western's grammar is used precisely and in Sesotho, and the second taking is what makes the film more than a transposition: the question of who holds ground outlives the regime that made it a question. It is the strongest evidence in the pack that the form travels to places whose own history supplies the plot.

entries.category: The Brazilian and Latin American Western
entries.name: O Cangaceiro
entries.author: dir. Lima Barreto
entries.awards: Won the International Award for Best Adventure Film at Cannes in 1953; the score received a special mention rather than a prize, which is a distinction the usual account loses.
entries.description: Sertão land, a band of cangaceiros and the volante police column hunting them — the nordestern's founding film and the one that carried the…
entries.text: Sertão land, a band of cangaceiros and the volante police column hunting them — the nordestern's founding film and the one that carried the tradition abroad under a name European audiences could file. The cangaceiro is the tradition's own figure rather than a borrowed one, which is why the pack admits the Brazilian material on principle rather than by exception. Its commercial success in Europe is the reason the sertão westerns were made at all.

entries.category: The Brazilian and Latin American Western
entries.name: Deus e o Diabo na Terra do Sol
entries.author: dir. Glauber Rocha
entries.awards: None (verified negative; it competed at Cannes in 1964).
entries.description: Released in English as Black God, White Devil. A cowherd kills the landowner who cheated him over cattle and walks into a landscape offering him a…
entries.text: Released in English as Black God, White Devil. A cowherd kills the landowner who cheated him over cattle and walks into a landscape offering him a prophet and then a bandit, neither of which is an answer. Everything follows from a contested claim to stock and ground, and Rocha's stated acquisitions of Ford and Leone are then inverted: the ballad narrating it belongs to the people rather than to the film. It is Cinema Novo's central text and the sertão's whole argument in one picture.

entries.category: The Brazilian and Latin American Western
entries.name: El Topo
entries.author: dir. Alejandro Jodorowsky
entries.description: A gunfighter's progress through a Mexican desert as a sequence of duels that are also a religious argument, and the film on which the term acid…
entries.text: A gunfighter's progress through a Mexican desert as a sequence of duels that are also a religious argument, and the film on which the term acid western was later built. It is second mode throughout: the genre's furniture is used against the settlement argument rather than in service of it, and competence is the thing being dismantled. Jodorowsky's own statements about the production include a claim of rape made in the book of the film, a 2007 revision of that claim and a later description of it as invented provocation; all three positions are on the record, the pack states all three and adjudicates none.
